title: Filter employees whose email domain is "gmail.com".
shortTitle: Filter employees whose email domain is "gmail.com"
keyPoints: Use String.endsWith("@gmail.com") to check the domain, including the @ sign to avoid false matches.
Without the @ sign, an address like someone@notgmail.com would wrongly match a plain gmail.com suffix.
Splitting on @ and comparing index 1 with equalsIgnoreCase is more precise for case-insensitive matching.
Always guard against null emails with a null check first, relying on short-circuit evaluation.
Pattern.compile(regex).asPredicate() or asMatchPredicate() converts a regex to a reusable Predicate.
For anything beyond a simple domain check, use a vetted library for full email validation.
Email domains are case-insensitive by RFC standard, so lower-case or use equalsIgnoreCase.

s1_definition.oneliner: Filter on endsWith("@gmail.com") including the @ sign to avoid false matches like notgmail.com, and guard against null with short-circuit evaluation.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **endsWith("@gmail.com")** – checks the domain portion including the @ to prevent false positives.
- **Split approach** – `email.split("@")[1].equalsIgnoreCase("gmail.com")` is more precise for case-insensitive matching.
- **Null guard** – `e.email() != null && e.email().endsWith(...)` uses short-circuit to avoid NPE.
- **Case sensitivity** – email domains are case-insensitive by RFC, so lower-case before comparing or use equalsIgnoreCase.
- **Regex alternative** – `Pattern.compile(".*@gmail\\.com$").asPredicate()` for pattern-based matching.
s1_definition.analogy: The compliance officer at National Bank of India says, 'List every employee who registered a personal Gmail address so we can remind them to use the official bank email.' The clerk checks each address and keeps the ones ending in @gmail.com.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Email domain filter:
  ────────────────────
  Input: rajesh@gmail.com      endsWith("@gmail.com") → true  ✓
  Input: priya@bank.co.in      endsWith("@gmail.com") → false ✗
  Input: amit@Gmail.COM        toLowerCase → @gmail.com → true  ✓
  Input: null                  null check → skip       ✗
  Input: vikram@notgmail.com   endsWith("@gmail.com") → false ✗
                               (@ anchors the boundary)
  Result: [Rajesh, Amit]
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
To filter by email domain, use endsWith with the full suffix including the @ sign. Without the @, an address at notgmail.com would wrongly match. Guard against null emails with a null check first, relying on short-circuit evaluation.

Email domains are case-insensitive by RFC standard, so lower-case the address before comparing or use equalsIgnoreCase. The split approach isolates the domain part precisely and handles edge cases like malformed addresses.

For complex pattern matching, Pattern.compile().asPredicate() converts a regex to a reusable, thread-safe Predicate. For anything beyond a simple domain check, use a vetted library for full email validation.

Remember one sentence: include the @ sign in endsWith to anchor the domain boundary, guard against null, and lower-case for case-insensitive matching.
